Subject: Re: Great chat earlier - tokens vs characters vs requests (worked example)

Hi Alicia - quick note from the SE side to clarify tokens vs characters vs requests and how caching affects billing. TL;DR: requests != billed tokens; characters are an approximation - tokens are the billing unit. Example math below so you can see where the costs come from.

Key points:
- Request = one API call (how many times your app hits the model).
- Billed tokens = tokenized input (prompt) + tokenized output (response). We bill per-token.
- Characters -> tokens: rough rule-of-thumb is 3-5 characters per token depending on language; use ~4 chars/token for English as a conservative average.

Worked example using your numbers (ballpark):
- Avg prompt: 400 chars -> ~100 tokens (400 / 4).
- Avg response: 800 chars -> ~200 tokens.
- Total per request: ~300 tokens.
- At 1.2M requests/month -> 1.2M * 300 = 360M tokens/month.

What that means for unit economics:
- If you want to evaluate target $/1M tokens, compute: (monthly tokens / 1,000,000) * $/1M.
- Example: if target is $200 per 1M tokens -> monthly cost = 360 * $200 = $72,000 (illustrative - dedicated reserved pricing will be much lower per 1M in committed tiers).

How caching changes billed tokens (prefix caching):
- Full-request caching only helps when the entire prompt+context is identical - not likely in your case.
- Prefix or KV caching helps when a repeated template/prompt prefix is the same across requests and only a small variable is appended. With prefix caching Redwood can avoid re-sending the repeated prefix tokens to the model on every request and instead send a smaller delta.
- Example with 35% templated prefixes: if template prefix = 60 tokens and only patient-specific context = 40 tokens changes per request, caching avoids re-billing the 60 tokens each time after the cache warms.
  - Baseline: 300 tokens/request -> 360M tokens/month
  - With prefix caching (35% of requests see prefix saved): saved tokens = 1.2M * 35% * 60 = 25.2M tokens/month saved (~7% reduction).
  - Combined with response-size optimizations and batching, realistic reductions can be 10-35% depending on workload.

Other levers to reach your budget target:
- Shorten prompts where possible (template + structured fields instead of free text).
- Use lower-cost model variants or quantized models for production inference.
- Consider Dedicated / Reserved capacity if steady-state volume - Redwood Dedicated has lower $/1M in committed tiers.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Share 10 sample prompt/response pairs and we will tokenize them and return an exact monthly token estimate.
2) If budget is the blocker, we can run two scenarios: hosted with caching and a dedicated committed tier (I can run the math once we have tokenized samples).

Happy to sync live for 20 minutes to walk through the numbers.
